name: Isracard
why_it_matters: Largest of Israel's three card companies (issuer and acquirer): NIS 3,150M revenue in 2024, ranked first by DUNS100; historically the sole clearer of Isracard and Mastercard brand transactions until the regulator opened clearing to competition.
typical_access: direct, or through an Israeli gateway (PayPlus, Grow, Cardcom, Tranzila, Hyp) that routes to the card companies

name: Cal (ICC-Cal / Visa Cal)
why_it_matters: Second of the three card companies: NIS 2,883M revenue in 2024 and the highest profitability of the three (15.6% net margin, DUNS100); a 72% stake sale to Union Investments and Harel was signed in September 2025, pending regulatory approval (GlobalData).
typical_access: direct, or through an Israeli gateway

name: Max
why_it_matters: Third card company (NIS 2,118M revenue in 2024, DUNS100). Owns the CreditGuard gateway, bought from Nuvei/SafeCharge for NIS 70M in 2020; that deal gave Nuvei merchants a route to Max's acquiring in Israel (Globes).
typical_access: direct, via CreditGuard gateway, or via Nuvei (per 2020 partnership announcement)

name: PayPlus
why_it_matters: Israeli clearing gateway that works with all Israeli credit card companies; supports cards, Bit, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank transfer and recurring payments; claims 'tens of thousands of businesses' and ships Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce, SAP and Oracle integrations. No public share figure found. This is the provider adidas named for Israel.
typical_access: direct (gateway contract plus merchant accounts with the card companies)

name: Grow (formerly Meshulam)
why_it_matters: Licensed Israeli payment company: claims 100,000+ businesses, 1,000+ new customers a month and more than NIS 6B a year processed; accepts cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Bit, PayBox and bank transfer; Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce and Wix plugins.

name: Cardcom
why_it_matters: Israeli clearing company that is both acquirer and gateway ('one stop shop'); claims tens of thousands of businesses and billions of shekels cleared per month; cards (Visa, Mastercard, Diners), Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal and Bit; WooCommerce and Shopify plugins. No public share figure found.

name: Tranzila
why_it_matters: One of the oldest Israeli online gateways (founded 1999 per a partner case study) and a Shopify payment app for Israel; works on top of the merchant's acquiring contract with a card company; sells Bit as an add-on. No public share figure found.
typical_access: direct (gateway on top of the merchant's card-company contract)

name: Hyp (Hyp Pay)
why_it_matters: Israeli gateway with hosted payment page and enterprise APIs; its docs state that splitting payments into installments is 'very common' in Israel and expose both interest-free and credit installments. No public share figure found.

name: Nuvei
why_it_matters: Global PSP with Israeli roots (ex-SafeCharge). Announced in 2020 a strategic partnership with Max under which Nuvei merchants can connect to Max's acquiring services in Israel. No current public statement on local ILS acquiring found.

name: Cards (with installments / tashlumim)
why_it_matters: Cards are 71% of Israeli e-commerce value (PPRO country page, published 2024): Visa 37%, Mastercard 26%, local schemes 16%, Amex 6%. Splitting into interest-free monthly installments at checkout is 'very common' (Hyp docs) and expected by shoppers.
typical_access: direct via the three card companies or any Israeli gateway

name: Local card schemes / Isracard-branded cards
why_it_matters: Local schemes are 16% of card volume in Israel (PPRO); Isracard is the domestic brand issued by Isracard and historically cleared only by it.
typical_access: via Isracard acquiring or an Israeli gateway

name: Bit (Bank Hapoalim)
why_it_matters: Bank Hapoalim's payment app: 3.5 million customers and about 90% of app-based payment transfers (Globes, July 2024); pays on websites and apps without entering card details. E-wallets are 26% of Israeli e-commerce (PPRO).
typical_access: via Israeli gateways (PayPlus, Grow, Cardcom, Tranzila list Bit)

name: Apple Pay / Google Pay
why_it_matters: Stripe's Israel guide notes many Israelis use Apple Pay and Google Pay alongside local apps; every major Israeli gateway (PayPlus, Grow, Cardcom) lists both. Part of the 26% e-wallet share (PPRO); no separate share figure found.

name: PayBox (Discount Bank)
why_it_matters: Second P2P payment app: 1.4 million customers and about 10% of app transfers (Globes, July 2024); accepted by Grow and other gateways.

name: BNPL (Splitit, Sunbit, Jifiti)
why_it_matters: Stripe's guide names Splitit, Jifiti and Sunbit Israel as BNPL providers and cites a BNPL market of US$1.37B in 2025; card installments remain the mainstream way to split purchases.
